newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop 2.11 pct on bank sector sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop 2.11 pct on bank sector sales.

text.p: Thai stocks ended 2.11 percent lower on Thursday as continued offloading of shares of ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc spurred sales of bank stocks and depressed the market, traders said.
After dipping as low as 695.57, the SET Index ended the day down 15.13 points at 701.76. The SET 50 closed 0.50 points, or 0.93 percent lower, at 53.48. Turnover was 2.96 billion baht.
"The BBC sales was the main negative factor hurting the banking sector. Trade was driven by sentiment more than fundamentals," said a General Finance trader.

Bangkok Bank of Commerce shares resumed trading on Thursday after an 11-month suspension. The bank topped the active list, plunging 12.30 baht to 3.70. The stock decline was not restrained by a 10 percent floor limit on the first day of its resumed trade.
The bank was saddled with huge non-performing loans and it faced uncertain future despite a central bank organised attempt to revive its operation.
